title: ResourceLoader failing to load SubResource of inner class
body:
### Tested versions

v4.6.1.rc1.official [7bfffc846]

### System information

Ubuntu

### Issue description

When serializing state defined in an inner class, the `ResourceLoader` fails to load it.

[This is all](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_basics.html#inner-classes) I could find in terms of documentation on inner classes, which if I didn't miss something, is extremely sparse and does not mention any peculiarities in terms of using `@export`.

### Steps to reproduce

We have a resource such as this:

```gd
extends Resource
class_name MyResource

@export var state_a: int
@export var state_b: MyStruct

class MyStruct extends Resource:
	@export var state: int
```

We instantiate it, assign some values, and serialize it via `ResourceSaver`. Here's the result:

```
[gd_resource type="Resource" script_class="MyResource" format=3]

[ext_resource type="Script" path="res://my_resource.gd" id="1_ut6f4"]

[sub_resource type="GDScript" id="GDScript_cg3k6"]

[sub_resource type="Resource" id="Resource_a0755"]
script = SubResource("GDScript_cg3k6")
state = 321321

[resource]
script = ExtResource("1_ut6f4")
state_a = 123123
state_b = SubResource("Resource_a0755")
```

This looks just fine to me, the state defined by the inner class has been serialized: `state = 321321`

Now we attempt to load our file using `ResoruceLoader`.

Regrettably, what should be an instance of our inner class comes up as `null`.

If instead we declared the property holding our inner class instance like this:
```
@export var state_b := MyStruct.new()
```
then we do get a valid instance, but its `state` property comes up as `0` when it should have been overwritten by the read state (from tres file).

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[godot_4_inner_class_export.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25320554/godot_4_inner_class_export.zip)
